title: Harimoto recovers from two games down to beat Li Tianyang for Asian title
standfirst: Japan's world No. 3 lost the first two games of the men's singles final in Tashkent, then took the next three to deny China a clean sweep of the men's events.

image.alt: Tomokazu Harimoto playing at the Paris 2024 Olympics
image.caption: Harimoto at Paris 2024

body: Tomokazu Harimoto is the Asian men's singles champion after coming back from two games down against Li Tianyang in Tashkent on Sunday. The Chinese player won the opening game 11-1 and edged the second 11-9, but Harimoto took the next three 11-7, 11-8, 11-7 to win the final of the 2026 Asian Championships.

Harimoto's route to the final was far less fraught. He beat China's Wen Ruibo 3-0 in the semi-finals, dropping no more than seven points in any game. Li needed five games to get past Chinese Taipei's Kuo Guan-hong in the other semi-final, coming through 11-6 in the decider after Kuo had taken the first game 13-11.

The result denied China a clean sweep of the men's events. Lin Shidong and Huang Youzheng won the men's doubles, beating compatriots Wen Ruibo and Yuan Licen 3-1 in an all-Chinese final, and China's men had already retained their team title earlier in the week with a 3-0 win over Korea.

Across the tournament, China and Japan shared all seven titles, four to three, according to Butterfly's report from Uzbekistan. Japan's other wins came in the women's team event and the mixed doubles, where Miwa Harimoto, Tomokazu's sister, partnered world No. 1 Sora Matsushima to gold. China's Chen Yi beat Miwa Harimoto 3-0 in the women's singles final, and Kuai Man and Wang Yidi won the women's doubles.

Harimoto went into the week ranked third in the world behind Matsushima and France's Félix Lebrun. The championships, held from 19 to 25 October, also decided Asian qualification places for next year's World Championships in Astana.
His next test comes quickly. WTT Champions Montpellier starts on Tuesday, where organisers have promised most of the men's top 10, though without the injured Wang Chuqin.
